claims.claim: C1: Age-dependent posterior re-weighting of provisionally-clean commits (LAW) improves online JIT-SDP over waiting-time baselines
closest_prior: Liu et al. 2024a (PU learning for JIT-SDP) - primary source UNVERIFIED/not found; treated as prior art for the generic PU framing
claims.exact_difference: ODaSC derives label confidence from feature-space micro-clusters for examples already labelled clean after W days; LAW derives it from commit age via a right-truncation-corrected discovery-delay distribution combined with model risk, and also trains on commits younger than W. Difference vs CVR methods: domain transfer + truncation-aware nonparametric delay estimate (weaker).
claims.status: open - generic PU framing conceded to prior art (Liu 2024a, unverified); claim narrowed to age/delay-based weighting in online setting; ODaSC to be baseline in plan_v2

claims.claim: C2 (Type A/C): waiting time barely denoises labels; its effect is mainly class-composition shift of recent data
claims.status: model-free evidence on 14 projects; needs a model-based confirmation (E3 diag)

claims.claim: C3: latency-corrected, per-update G-mean threshold calibration (no tuned rate) for online JIT-SDP
closest_prior: Pessoa 2021 fixed defect prediction rate (tuned fr1, rate-driven threshold)
ORB (Cabral 2019) boosting toward a target prediction rate th
threshold-choice theory (Hernandez-Orallo, Flach, Ferri 2012) - NOT YET OPENED
claims.exact_difference: Pessoa and ORB steer predictions toward a FIXED target rate tuned offline; ours chooses the threshold at every update from the model's own past scores against labels corrected for verification latency (truncation-corrected delay survival), with no target rate to tune.
claims.status: open; fr baseline enqueued (E0c); generic 'tune threshold on validation data' is standard ML - claim must be about the latency correction + online use

claims.claim: C4 (Type C insight): in online JIT-SDP the waiting time W acts largely as an operating-point (threshold) choice; at a calibrated threshold, G-mean sensitivity to W shrinks
closest_prior: Song, Minku, Yao 2023 EMSE (retrospective evaluation validity)
Pessoa 2021 (fixed prediction rate as baseline for class imbalance evolution)
claims.exact_difference: Prior work treats W as trading label noise against staleness; we show (dev so far) best-threshold G-mean varies little across W while 0.5-threshold G-mean varies hugely.
claims.status: dev evidence only (2 projects, seed 0); needs E0b across 4 dev projects and test confirmation
